changes.before: Eleven blood samples of a drug with true half-life 5 h (dashed green line) are generated with lognormal assay noise. The accent line is the least-squares fit; its shaded band is the nominal 95 % interval for the slope. Choose whether to **keep the earliest or the latest** $n$ samples and slide $n$: the right panel plots the estimated half-life with its nominal 95 % interval for every $n$ (current one in gold). **New sample** draws fresh noise. Samples under the assay limit of 0.1 mg/L (hollow) are not reported. This outcome-dependent exclusion breaks the uncensored Gaussian pivot assumptions; the displayed intervals then have no exact 95 % coverage guarantee.
changes.after: Eleven blood samples of a drug with true half-life 5 h (dashed green line) are generated with lognormal assay noise. The accent line is the least-squares fit; its shaded band is the nominal 95 % interval for the slope. Choose whether to **keep the earliest or the latest** $n$ samples and slide $n$: the right panel plots the estimated half-life with its nominal 95 % interval for every $n$ (current one in gold). **New sample** draws fresh noise. Samples under the assay limit of 0.1 mg/L (hollow) are not reported. This outcome-dependent exclusion breaks the uncensored Gaussian pivot assumptions; the displayed intervals then have no exact 95 % coverage guarantee. The right panel displays 0–30 h only: finite endpoints inside the range have caps; a top ∞ marks an unbounded upper endpoint and a top > a finite upper endpoint above 30 h. P> marks a positive point estimate above 30 h that is omitted from the plotted points. A bottom × means that the rate interval contains no positive elimination rate; nonpositive point estimates are omitted. These glyphs are status labels, not finite half-life estimates.
